contributors.name: Throughput
contributors.summary: Check whether the flow change is corroborated by the process and an independent indication before treating it as a process change.

steps.action: Confirm the timestamp, engineering units, meter status/quality, and whether the value is instantaneous flow or a totalized/rate value. Review recent maintenance or configuration changes.
steps.distinguishes: A stale, invalid, mis-scaled, or differently defined signal from an actual flow change.
steps.escalate: If status is bad, units are uncertain, or a configuration change is unexplained, involve instrumentation/control staff before using the value for decisions.

steps.action: Compare the indication with an independent flow measurement or flow-computer value, if available, and with the operating log. Compare related suction/discharge pressure, speed, and load trends at the same timestamps.
steps.distinguishes: A change affecting the process from a single-tag measurement or data-path issue; correlated trends help locate where the process change may begin.
steps.escalate: Escalate a sustained mismatch or a flow change associated with equipment alarms or protective events under the site procedure.

steps.action: Ask the control-room operator to verify the approved lineup and operating demand from the control system. Do not operate valves or open a meter body as a diagnostic step.
steps.distinguishes: A documented operating transition from an unexplained measurement shift.
steps.escalate: Use the site change-management and permit/isolation processes for any field inspection or adjustment; engineering/instrumentation review is appropriate if the cause remains unclear.

contributors.name: Suction pressure
contributors.summary: Corroborate suction pressure against the upstream header and another indication; distinguish a supply/process change from an instrument-path issue.

steps.action: Check transmitter health/status, timestamp, range, units, and recent calibration/configuration or maintenance history. Compare with a second indication or approved local gauge when available.
steps.distinguishes: An invalid, shifted, or incorrectly ranged signal from a real pressure change.
steps.escalate: Request instrumentation review if indications disagree, status is abnormal, or the range/configuration cannot be confirmed.

steps.action: Trend suction pressure against the upstream supply/header and the neighboring equipment, plus throughput, speed, and discharge pressure. Check existing alarm/event history.
steps.distinguishes: An upstream supply or common-header change from a local compressor or measurement issue.
steps.escalate: Follow the approved low-suction, surge, and protective-action procedures if their site-defined alarms/events occur; do not wait for this diagnostic sequence.

steps.action: Have authorized personnel review the pressure connection/impulse path and any associated isolation or manifold status using the equipment manual and site permit/isolation rules. Do not loosen a pressurized fitting.
steps.distinguishes: A blocked, leaking, or isolated measurement connection from a process pressure change.
steps.escalate: Any inspection requiring process contact, opening a fitting, or electrical work requires the applicable site authorization and isolation.

contributors.name: RPM
contributors.summary: Compare the displayed speed with controller demand and an independent speed indication, where safely available; do not approach rotating equipment.

steps.action: Check the speed tag timestamp, quality/status, units, controller demand, driver status, and event/alarm history. Compare with an independent approved speed indication if one is available.
steps.distinguishes: A speed pickup/transmission or display problem from a real change in shaft speed or control demand.
steps.escalate: Escalate disagreement, bad quality, overspeed/underspeed alarm, trip, or abnormal vibration immediately through the site response procedure.

steps.action: Have authorized controls/instrument personnel review the pickup diagnostics, signal path, and recent maintenance/configuration history against the exact installed driver and sensor manuals.
steps.distinguishes: A sensor, wiring, configuration, or controller signal issue from a driver/load/control issue.
steps.escalate: Do not inspect wiring or sensor installation near operating machinery; electrical and mechanical work requires site authorization and isolation as applicable.

steps.action: Compare speed with load, throughput, and pressure trends and ask operations to confirm the intended operating mode from records.
steps.distinguishes: A process/load transition from an isolated speed indication or control anomaly.
steps.escalate: Do not adjust governor, speed demand, overspeed trip, or protective settings as troubleshooting. Refer unexplained changes to operations and the responsible engineering/maintenance group.

contributors.name: Discharge pressure
contributors.summary: Compare discharge and downstream pressure trends before deciding whether backpressure or the measurement channel is the stronger lead.

steps.action: Verify tag identity, timestamp, units, transmitter status/range, and recent maintenance or configuration history. Compare with an independent indication if available.
steps.distinguishes: A data-quality, configuration, or instrument problem from a process pressure change.
steps.escalate: Ask instrumentation/control staff to investigate if readings conflict, the status is abnormal, or the calibration/configuration is uncertain.

steps.action: Compare discharge pressure with downstream header pressure, related unit indications, suction pressure, temperature, throughput, speed, and existing alarms/events.
steps.distinguishes: A downstream restriction/backpressure pattern or operating transition from a localized transmitter anomaly; correlated measurements provide context, not proof.
steps.escalate: Follow site-defined high-pressure, temperature, vibration, or protective-event procedures immediately when applicable.

steps.action: Ask the control-room operator to verify approved valve lineup and control response from existing indications and logs. Do not move a valve, alter a setpoint, or change protection logic to test a hypothesis.
steps.distinguishes: A documented lineup/control change from an unexplained pressure trend.
steps.escalate: Route suspected restriction, control malfunction, or repeated abnormal pressure to operations and engineering under site procedures; field checks require applicable permits/isolation.

contributors.name: Slug catcher level
contributors.summary: Check level indication quality and corroborate accumulation with an independent indication and process context; use site high-level response procedures for alarms.

steps.action: Confirm timestamp, percent scale/range, level transmitter status, and recent calibration/configuration or maintenance history. Compare with an independent local indication where installed and safe to read.
steps.distinguishes: A scaling, stale-signal, or instrument problem from a real level change.
steps.escalate: If the indications disagree or instrument status is abnormal, request instrumentation review; do not enter or open process equipment to verify level.

steps.action: Trend level with upstream liquid/process conditions, inflow/outflow indicators, and existing alarm/event history. Review control-system indication of the level controller and dump-valve feedback without changing commands.
steps.distinguishes: Accumulation or changing liquid handling from a sensor/feedback problem; feedback is not proof of actual valve movement.
steps.escalate: At site-defined high/high-high alarms, suspected carryover, or protective events, follow the approved response immediately and notify operations.

steps.action: Ask authorized operations/maintenance personnel to verify the approved liquid-handling lineup and instrument installation history. Do not manually drain, bypass, or force a valve based on this anomaly summary.
steps.distinguishes: A documented operating change from unexplained level behavior.
steps.escalate: Any field action must follow approved procedures, permits, isolation, and environmental controls; escalate suspected carryover or loss of containment without delay.

steps.distinguishes: A stale, invalid, mis-scaled, or differently defined signal from an actual flow change.
steps.escalate: If status is bad, units are uncertain, or a configuration change is unexplained, involve instrumentation/control staff before using the value for decisions.

steps.action: Compare the indication with an independent flow measurement or flow-computer value, if available, and with the operating log. Compare related suction/discharge pressure, speed, and load trends at the same timestamps.
steps.distinguishes: A change affecting the process from a single-tag measurement or data-path issue; correlated trends help locate where the process change may begin.
steps.escalate: Escalate a sustained mismatch or a flow change associated with equipment alarms or protective events under the site procedure.

steps.action: Ask the control-room operator to verify the approved lineup and operating demand from the control system. Do not operate valves or open a meter body as a diagnostic step.
steps.distinguishes: A documented operating transition from an unexplained measurement shift.
steps.escalate: Use the site change-management and permit/isolation processes for any field inspection or adjustment; engineering/instrumentation review is appropriate if the cause remains unclear.

contributors.name: Discharge pressure
contributors.summary: Compare discharge and downstream pressure trends before deciding whether backpressure or the measurement channel is the stronger lead.

steps.action: Verify tag identity, timestamp, units, transmitter status/range, and recent maintenance or configuration history. Compare with an independent indication if available.
steps.distinguishes: A data-quality, configuration, or instrument problem from a process pressure change.
steps.escalate: Ask instrumentation/control staff to investigate if readings conflict, the status is abnormal, or the calibration/configuration is uncertain.

steps.action: Compare discharge pressure with downstream header pressure, related unit indications, suction pressure, temperature, throughput, speed, and existing alarms/events.
steps.distinguishes: A downstream restriction/backpressure pattern or operating transition from a localized transmitter anomaly; correlated measurements provide context, not proof.
steps.escalate: Follow site-defined high-pressure, temperature, vibration, or protective-event procedures immediately when applicable.

steps.action: Ask the control-room operator to verify approved valve lineup and control response from existing indications and logs. Do not move a valve, alter a setpoint, or change protection logic to test a hypothesis.
steps.distinguishes: A documented lineup/control change from an unexplained pressure trend.
steps.escalate: Route suspected restriction, control malfunction, or repeated abnormal pressure to operations and engineering under site procedures; field checks require applicable permits/isolation.

contributors.name: RPM
contributors.summary: Compare the displayed speed with controller demand and an independent speed indication, where safely available; do not approach rotating equipment.

steps.action: Check the speed tag timestamp, quality/status, units, controller demand, driver status, and event/alarm history. Compare with an independent approved speed indication if one is available.
steps.distinguishes: A speed pickup/transmission or display problem from a real change in shaft speed or control demand.
steps.escalate: Escalate disagreement, bad quality, overspeed/underspeed alarm, trip, or abnormal vibration immediately through the site response procedure.

steps.action: Have authorized controls/instrument personnel review the pickup diagnostics, signal path, and recent maintenance/configuration history against the exact installed driver and sensor manuals.
steps.distinguishes: A sensor, wiring, configuration, or controller signal issue from a driver/load/control issue.
steps.escalate: Do not inspect wiring or sensor installation near operating machinery; electrical and mechanical work requires site authorization and isolation as applicable.

steps.action: Compare speed with load, throughput, and pressure trends and ask operations to confirm the intended operating mode from records.
steps.distinguishes: A process/load transition from an isolated speed indication or control anomaly.
steps.escalate: Do not adjust governor, speed demand, overspeed trip, or protective settings as troubleshooting. Refer unexplained changes to operations and the responsible engineering/maintenance group.

contributors.name: Suction pressure
contributors.summary: Corroborate suction pressure against the upstream header and another indication; distinguish a supply/process change from an instrument-path issue.

steps.action: Check transmitter health/status, timestamp, range, units, and recent calibration/configuration or maintenance history. Compare with a second indication or approved local gauge when available.
steps.distinguishes: An invalid, shifted, or incorrectly ranged signal from a real pressure change.
steps.escalate: Request instrumentation review if indications disagree, status is abnormal, or the range/configuration cannot be confirmed.

steps.action: Trend suction pressure against the upstream supply/header and the neighboring equipment, plus throughput, speed, and discharge pressure. Check existing alarm/event history.
steps.distinguishes: An upstream supply or common-header change from a local compressor or measurement issue.
steps.escalate: Follow the approved low-suction, surge, and protective-action procedures if their site-defined alarms/events occur; do not wait for this diagnostic sequence.

steps.action: Have authorized personnel review the pressure connection/impulse path and any associated isolation or manifold status using the equipment manual and site permit/isolation rules. Do not loosen a pressurized fitting.
steps.distinguishes: A blocked, leaking, or isolated measurement connection from a process pressure change.
steps.escalate: Any inspection requiring process contact, opening a fitting, or electrical work requires the applicable site authorization and isolation.
